hero_alt: MyPolly, a pollinator house in a garden
contesto_body: MyPolly was born inside 3Bee: a physical product that brings pollinators into people’s gardens and balconies. A simple object, behind which sits a complex topic — biodiversity — that the audience barely knew.
The project started with no e-commerce history: no internal benchmarks, no existing funnel, an audience yet to be built.
sfida_statement: Selling a product people weren’t searching for: turning biodiversity into *an everyday purchase.*
sfida_body: The price sat above the category average, and the benefit — more pollinators, more biodiversity — is neither immediate nor visible. The conversation had to move from the cost of the object to the value of the gesture: educate before selling, build trust before the funnel.

ruolo_attivita.descrizione: Defining the message and the value proposition: what makes MyPolly a gesture for biodiversity, not a garden accessory.
Designing the purchase journey: educational content at the top, targeted advertising, landing pages built for people discovering the topic for the first time.
An editorial plan that explains the why before the what: biodiversity as a story to understand, not a technical spec.
Activating the community: buyers join the project, with impact updates and reasons to come back.

strategia_paragrafo: Instead of squeezing the price, we raised the perceived value: content that explains the impact, a funnel that educates before it asks, a community that turns customers into advocates. The results came when the audience stopped comparing MyPolly with other garden objects — and started comparing it with their own impact.

risultati.descrizione: at the moments of highest campaign traction
growth of the active community during the launch period

cosa_dimostra: A high-value product isn’t sold by lowering the price, but by raising understanding: strategy, education and community can turn a niche topic into an everyday purchase.
